title: Stack (LIFO)
intuition: Last-In, First-Out: the most recently added element is always the first one removed.
whyExists: Many computational processes need to remember nested states and backtrack in reverse order: function call stacks, undo/redo buffers, and bracket matching.
analogy: A spring-loaded plate dispenser in a cafeteria: you can only push a clean plate on top, and you can only take the top plate off.
coreIdea: A Stack restricts insertions and deletions to a single end called the TOP. Both push() and pop() operate in strictly $O(1)$ time because no internal elements ever shift.

complexity.reason: All modifications happen strictly at the top index without memory relocation.

pitfalls: Stack Overflow: pushing onto a fixed-capacity stack that is full.
Stack Underflow: attempting to pop or peek from an empty stack without checking isEmpty().
Violating LIFO discipline by attempting random access to middle elements.
